thread.title_full: Woman confesses to slaying second spouse in Southern California - NewsBreak

author: Josh DuBose
title: Woman confesses to slaying second spouse in Southern California - NewsBreak
text:
By Josh DuBose ,
2 hours ago
A 54-year-old woman who served nearly a decade in prison for killing her husband has pleaded guilty to killing her second spouse, a Cal Fire captain, last year.
Capt. Rebecca “Becky” Marodi , who was most recently assigned to the French Valley Cal Fire Station in Riverside County, was found by her mother on Feb. 17 suffering from multiple stab wounds to her neck, chest and back.
First responders were dispatched just before 9 p.m. to the 20200 block of Rancho Villa Road in the San Diego County community of Ramona. Despite life-saving measures, the 49-year-old died at the scene.
Days later, investigators obtained an arrest warrant for Marodi’s estranged wife, Yolanda Olejniczak Marodi.
Capt. Rebecca Marodi is shown in an undated photo. (Riverside County Fire Department Hazmat Team) A procession is held for Fire Capt. Rebecca Marodi after she was found fatally stabbed in her Ramona, California, home on Feb. 17, 2025. Authorities are investigating her death as a homicide. (KSWB/KUSI) Authorities said the domestic violence attack began around 8 p.m., less than an hour before sheriff’s deputies were called by Rebecca’s mother.
Detectives later reviewed home security footage that allegedly captured the attack. Investigators said Rebecca could be seen running from her attacker.
“Yolanda! Please! I don’t want to die!” she could be heard screaming.
According to investigators, Yolanda replied, “You should have thought of that before.”
About 75 minutes after the attack, Homeland Security records showed Yolanda crossing the border into Mexico. The following day, investigators said she messaged a known associate, writing, “Rebecca came home and told me she was leaving me. We had a big fight, and I hurt her. I’m sorry.”
Yolanda Marodi was previously incarcerated from 2004 to 2013 under the name Yolanda Olejniczak after being convicted of voluntary manslaughter in the 2000 stabbing death of her then-husband, Jim Olejniczak, in Riverside County.
Yolanda Marodi, also known as Yolanda Olejniczak, is suspected of fatally stabbing her wife, Rebecca Marodi. (San Diego County Crime Stoppers) Yolanda Marodi held in custody in Baja California, Mexico. (Secretaria De Seguridad Ciudadana de Baja California) Yolanda Olenjniczak is pictured in an undated photo. Olenjniczak has been identified as a suspect in the fatal stabbing of Cal Fire Capt. Rebecca Marodi. (San Diego County Sheriff’s Office) On March 22, 2025, Mexican law enforcement officers arrested Yolanda in the Ferrocarril neighborhood of Mexicali near a hotel. She was later transferred to U.S. Marshals at a U.S. port of entry, processed and booked on suspicion of murder, according to the San Diego County Sheriff’s Office.
San Bernardino County deputy shot in Antelope Valley On Tuesday, Olejniczak Marodi admitted in San Diego Superior Court to killing Rebecca Marodi, the Los Angeles Times reported .
She pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and admitted using a knife in the killing.
Andrea Winter, a close friend of Rebecca’s, told The Times that Olejniczak Marodi was often jealous of Rebecca’s magnetic personality and that she noticed changes in her friend about a year before the killing.
Other friends told the newspaper they were unaware of Olejniczak Marodi’s criminal history but said she displayed controlling and isolating behavior before killing her estranged wife.
Olejniczak Marodi is scheduled to be sentenced Sept. 2 and could face 36 years to life in state prison.
